andrew_tate_extradition_fight:
By

Bill Chappell

Andrew Tate and Tristan Tate (obscured) — facing more than 50 charges in the U.K. and Romania, including rape and human trafficking — arrive in Florida after a travel ban on them was lifted in February 2025.
                
                    
                    Alon Skuy/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

After President Trump took office in 2025, Andrew Tate proclaimed, "The Tates will be free." It reflected an expectation that Trump would extricate the controversial 39-year-old influencer and his brother from legal troubles in Romania.

By then, Andrew Tate had spent years building political connections with the Trump family and other Republicans.

But now those ties are being tested: Andrew and Tristan Tate were arrested on July 18 and are now in a Florida prison, as the United Kingdom seeks to extradite them to face dozens of charges for serious crimes, including rape and human trafficking. The brothers, who are dual U.S.-British citizens, deny the charges and are fighting extradition.

It's a striking turnabout for the brothers, whose fans have included people who work in the U.S. government.

"The Tate brothers have friends on Capitol Hill," says Jared Holt, senior researcher at Open Measures, a company that monitors online extremism and disinformation. "There's people in the Trump administration that have cozied up to them before, people in the MAGA movement that have cozied up to them before, certainly."

Known for his polarizing views, Andrew Tate is one of the most famous faces of the international "manosphere" — a movement touting male dominance and extreme misogyny that has been embraced by some prominent voices in right-wing media.

"He is a huge star," Holt says of Tate.

But with a raft of criminal indictments in both the U.K. and Romania targeting Andrew and Tristan Tate, their support seems to be waning in the White House and fracturing elsewhere, according to analysts who study right-wing media.

"It seems like the [Trump] administration is trying to distance themselves a little bit now," says Kayla Gogarty, a research director at Media Matters. "But in general, we see some of the MAGA media kind of split" on the Tates.

The shift would reverse years of increasingly close ties between Andrew Tate and U.S. political players.

In 2017, Andrew Tate, a former kickboxer, was running a lucrative webcam porn business with his brother Tristan — an enterprise that would lead to accusations that the Tates coerced women to perform sex acts on camera and withheld their earnings from online work. Tate also faces charges related to indecent images of a child and extreme pornography.

Andrew Tate was banned from Twitter after saying of women: "If you put yourself in a position to be raped, you must bare some responsibility." Later, he was also blocked from platforms such as Instagram and TikTok.

"By 2022, Andrew Tate's banning turned him into a cause célèbre for supposed right-wing free speech advocates," conservative commentator Ben Shapiro — a noted Tate disdainer — recently said, "because Tate reframed his deplatforming as the political suppression of traditional masculinity."

The Tates grew their online porn business and began "Hustlers University" to sell "mentoring" lessons — geared to men — on how to make money. For a time, they offered what they called a "PhD" — or "Pimping Hoes Degree" — as noted by the Organized Crime and Corruption Reporting Project.

Andrew Tate (left) and his brother Tristan Tate speak during a protest against the Olympics next to the French Embassy in Bucharest, Romania, on July 28, 2024. The Tate brothers criticized the Paris 2024 Olympic Games for the inclusion message offered during the opening ceremony.
                
                    
                    Daniel Mihailescu/AFP via Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

Andrew Tate's popularity soared as he touted his lifestyle of luxury cars and dominating women, and said his critics were motivated by right-wing conspiracy ideas of "the Matrix" and the "deep state." Portraying himself as the target of globalist and "woke" forces, Tate appeared on popular podcasts such as Alex Jones, the Nelk Boys and Patrick Bet-David.

"I'm already still all over YouTube," he told Bet-David in September 2022. "But now I have a merit, I have a badge of … 'He's telling so much truth that they banned it.'"

In Google's 2023 Year in Search, Tate ranked just above French soccer star Kylian Mbappé as the third-most Googled person on Earth.

By then, the Tate brothers had relocated from the U.K. to Romania — where authorities arrested them in 2022 and charged them with human trafficking and rape. British police levied more sex-crime charges in early 2024 and later accused the brothers of dodging taxes on some 21 million pounds ($28 million, at today's exchange rate).

In the wake of the criminal charges in Romania, Tucker Carlson traveled there to interview Tate in July 2023, as did Candace Owens. At the time, Tate was under house arrest.

"I think they look at me and go, he's helping men resist the slave programming," Tate told Carlson. "We don't need him around; we need to empty their brains so we can inject the slave programming and convince men to be eunuchs, because once you're eunuched, then you're not a threat."

"I think I buy that," Carlson replied.

To Trump and other politicians, Holt says, Tate is a compelling figure because he offers access to a massive and energetic fanbase dominated by a desirable demographic: young men. And, Holt adds, some of the views Tate expresses align with Trump and his camp.

"It's like, here's a couple guys who are promoting the kind of ideals of hypermasculinity and machismo that we would like to promote," Holt says. "And they seem politically friendly, politically supportive of us. And they have this massive online audience."

Increasingly direct connections to the Trump camp emerged as Trump began his run to regain the presidency. When Trump launched his campaign in late 2022, those present at his Mar-a-Lago resort event included Joe McBride, the Tates' longtime lawyer who has also represented several Jan. 6 defendants.

In June 2024, Tate took part in a Twitter Spaces livestream with Donald Trump Jr., promoting a meme coin called MAGAA, according to a press release at the time.

That same month, during an episode of The Iced Coffee Hour podcast, influencer Justin Waller, a close business associate of Tate's, said he visited Mar-a-Lago, where he met and socialized with Barron Trump. At the time, Barron was helping his father's campaign connect with figures popular with Generation Z.

Barron Trump arrives at his father's inauguration in the Rotunda of the U.S. Capitol on Jan. 20, 2025, in Washington, D.C.
                
                    
                    Chip Somodevilla/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

"He knew the youth vote, you know, we won the youth vote by 36 points," Trump later said of his youngest son. "And he was saying, Dad, I, you gotta go out and do this one and that one," referring to interviews with influential podcasters such as Joe Rogan. (Trump did not win the youth vote overall, but did improve his margins with the voting block.)

"I'm very close with the Trump family. I know them well," Tate told reporters in Romania in July 2024. He added, "I spoke to Barron after the incident," referring to the assassination attempt on Trump days earlier in Butler, Pa.

As Tate's legal troubles grew in Romania and the U.K., he repeatedly posted about politics and said he was backing Trump's 2024 presidential run. Tate said online that he would donate $200,000 to Trump's campaign and told his followers on X, "God saved Trump from the bullet so you could vote for him."

Just ahead of Trump's inauguration in January 2025, Alina Habba, who was Trump's lawyer from 2021 until she joined his administration in 2025 as a counselor to the president and then as a federal prosecutor, appeared on conservative influencer Benny Johnson's Jan. 10 podcast along with Andrew Tate.

"I'm a big fan," Habba told Tate. She later added, "I admire what you're doing. I'm right there with you. And yeah, you're good. If you're in the States, I got your back."

Alina Habba speaks to reporters outside the White House on March 24, 2025, in Washington D.C.
                
                    
                    Win McNamee/Getty Images
                    
                
                hide caption

"When Donald Trump was reelected, there was a pretty rapid change in the disposition of the Romanian authorities towards the case," Heidi Blake, who wrote an investigative profile of Andrew Tate for The New Yorker, said in an interview with NPR.

"The Tates will be free, Trump is the president," Tate posted on X on Feb. 12, 2025. "The good old days are back. And they will be better than ever."

Two weeks later, Romania lifted a travel ban on Andrew and Tristan Tate, and they boarded a plane heading for America.

The move came after Euronews reported that the Trump administration expressed interest in the Tate brothers' case to Romanian authorities.

Romania's anti-organized crime agency, DIICOT, said prosecutors had approved a request to modify the Tates' travel ban. The agency did not specify who made the request.

The Tate brothers arrived in Florida in late February 2025. A week later, Andrew Tate appeared on the Trump-friendly Nelk Boys' Full Send Podcast.

"Thank the Lord Trump won," Tate said in that interview. "So we're kind of here because if things were different only a few months ago at that election, I have a strong suspicion I would be in a jail right now, and so would Trump."

But the president denied playing a role.

"I know nothing about that," Trump told reporters when he was asked if his administration had pressured Romania to allow the Tates to leave the country while under criminal indictment.

A number of Republicans balked at the Tates' presence, and some past supporters remained silent. The brothers arrived as Trump and other Republicans were under pressure to release a full accounting of the actions of convicted sex offender Jeffrey Epstein.

Florida Gov. Ron DeSantis expressed his displeasure immediately.

"I don't know how it came to this," DeSantis said of the Tates' arrival. "We were not involved, we were not notified."

Florida's Republican Attorney General James Uthmeier also reacted quickly: Within a week, he ordered state prosecutors "to execute search warrants and issue subpoenas" in a criminal investigation into the Tate brothers.

Still, the Tate brothers were benefiting from some support in powerful circles.

Democratic Sen. Richard Blumenthal of Connecticut and other lawmakers have called for an inquiry into a report from ProPublica that a Trump administration attorney named Paul Ingrassia, who formerly worked with McBride on the Tates' legal defense team, allegedly helped the brothers get back electronic devices that federal officers had seized when they entered the U.S.

And in March, the brothers attended a UFC event in Las Vegas — where UFC President and CEO Dana White, a longtime friend and ally of President Trump, warmly greeted them.

Andrew Tate attends a UFC 313 mixed martial arts event on March 8, 2025, in Las Vegas.
                
                    
                    John Locher/AP
                    
                
                hide caption

"Welcome to the States, boys," White said in a widely shared video.

This year, in mid-July, the brothers visited Washington, D.C., where it appeared they posed for a photo with Rep. Wesley Hunt, R-Texas. On the same trip, they were also spotted at a party hosted by Paolo Zampolli, a special envoy for Trump, according to The New York Times.

But then the U.K.'s extradition request arrived — and exposed a stark limit to the ties the Tates had fostered. U.S. marshals arrested Andrew and Tristan Tate in Florida on July 18.

The Trump administration has no plans to intervene in the Tate brothers' extradition battle, according to a terse statement by White House press secretary Karoline Leavitt on July 23. Many of their allies on the right have gone silent; a post on X from Rep. Abe Hamadeh, R-Ariz., stood out as he spoke against extraditing them.

To Russell Riley, a presidential historian at the University of Virginia, the Trump administration is doing what any previous administration in recent memory would have.

"Any properly acting White House chief of staff would have knocked in the head anybody who dared bring this within 50 feet of the Oval Office," he says of the Tates' extradition case.

In the days since, McBride, the Tates' lawyer, has sometimes vented anger at U.S. conservatives, accusing figures in the Trump administration and Washington of hating the Tates, without identifying them by name.

"The Political Right has a feminist problem," the lawyer posted on X on Aug. 1. "Andrew and Tristan Tate trigger them badly."

Still, politics could play a final role in the extradition process — and the fallout that would likely follow. One potential defense against extradition is the argument that criminal charges are politically motivated. And if the Tate brothers exhaust their legal challenges, their case would go to Secretary of State Marco Rubio for final review.

Editor's note: This story was updated to add the fact that President Trump did not win the youth vote in 2024 despite his claim to have done so. Aug. 12, 2026

Widdecombe's last public appearance

Former MP and MEP Ann Widdecombe was killed in a "targeted attack", counter terrorism police leading the investigation into her alleged murder have said.

The 78-year-old former Conservative minister turned Reform UK spokeswoman was found dead at her home in Devon on Thursday morning with serious injuries.

Police said on Saturday evening that they had arrested a 28-year-old man in Rotherham, South Yorkshire, on suspicion of her murder.

It later emerged the suspect had been seen in CCTV footage first obtained by the Sun, external appearing to get into a car in Yorkshire with what looks like a long object protruding from his pocket, hours before it is believed Widdecombe was attacked.

Devon and Cornwall Police initially said that, while they were keeping an open mind, there was "nothing to suggest" the murder was politically motivated. Counter terrorism police said on Tuesday "based on new information... it was appropriate that we took over the investigation".

Here is everything we know - and do not know - so far:

Police were pictured attending Ann Widdecombe's home on Dartmoor on Friday

Information unfolded over Friday and the weekend about what happened earlier in the week, including how and when Widdecombe died. Here is a timeline of events so far.

Wednesday 8 July

07:51 BST - CCTV footage appears to show a man dressed in a white shirt and shorts getting into a red vehicle outside a house in Rotherham, with what looks to be a long object protruding from his pocket

08:05 - Ann Widdecombe appears on TalkTV from her home in Haytor, a village on Dartmoor, to speak about her party Reform UK's leader Nigel Farage

12:19 - A researcher from Channel 5 reportedly speaks to Widdecombe looking to set up a video statement - her last message was received at 12:19

12.30 - Police believe this is the time that Widdecombe was attacked

12:48 - The Channel 5 researcher messages again, according to ITV reports, asking Widdecombe to join a Zoom link before the interview but she does not reply

Thursday 9 July

11:40 - Devon and Cornwall Police officers are called by the ambulance service and find Widdecombe dead in her home, with serious injuries

Friday 10 July

At around 06:30 - The BBC reports the announcement of Ann Widdecombe's death. A statement from her managing team does not have any information about when, how or where she had died and no detail to suggest her death was suspicious

At 15:44 - Police issue a statement saying they have launched a murder investigation. The force says there is "no information that this is a politically motivated crime" and also confirms the incident is not being treated as terror-related

At 16:13 - Widdecombe's management team releases a second statement saying they are "absolutely devastated" by the news of the police investigation following a "very traumatic and upsetting 24 hours"

At 17:45 - Devon and Cornwall Police Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman says at a press conference that a 26-year-old white British man has been arrested on suspicion of murder

Saturday 11 July

Shortly before 07:00 - Police say the suspect has been released from custody and is no longer part of their investigation. Police remain at the scene and a manhunt is under way as the force says the investigation is "moving at a significant pace"

The force say they are still searching for a suspect who they believe is a white male in connection with her death

At about 18:15, police say they have decided not to release further information, including descriptions of potential suspects or CCTV footage, for the time being as such information could "compromise ongoing enquiries"

Shortly before midnight, police said a 28-year-old white British national had been arrested in South Yorkshire by officers from Counter Terrorism Police North East and South Yorkshire Police

Sunday 12 July

Shortly after 11:30 - Police tell reporters there is nothing to suggest the alleged murder was politically motivated

They say they are not looking for anyone else in connection with the incident and that Widdecombe's family has been informed

Monday 13 July

Shortly before 13:00, Counter Terrorism Policing South East (CTPSE) confirms it is now leading the investigation into Widdecombe's death as "new information and evidence has come to light"

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood says she spoke to counter terrorism police and provided an update in the House of Commons on Monday afternoon

Mahmood told MPs that the suspect was not known to Prevent - the government's anti-extremism scheme

Tuesday 14 July

Devon and Cornwall's police and crime commissioner acknowledges "commentary" about the way police communicated during the early stages of the case but defends the force, saying its response was "substantial and professional"

Head of Counter Terrorism Policing Assistant Commissioner Laurence Taylor tells reporters Widdecombe had been killed in a "targeted attack" - and says detectives are still working to understand the motive

Police say Ann Widdecombe killed in 'targeted attack' as motive investigated

Village in shock as 'horrific' Ann Widdecombe murder case unfolds

Ann Widdecombe obituary: Brexit-backing former minister turned Strictly star

A 26-year-old white British man was arrested on Friday on suspicion of the murder of Widdecombe. He was arrested in Newton Abbot, a town roughly 10 miles from Haytor.

However, on Saturday morning, Devon and Cornwall Police said the man had been released from custody and was no longer part of the investigation.

Shortly before midnight on Saturday, police said they had arrested a 28-year-old man in South Yorkshire on suspicion of murder.

"The suspect, who is a white British national, is now in police custody," the statement from Devon and Cornwall police said.

On Sunday, Assistant Chief Constable Matt Longman said officers remained "open-minded" about a potential motive and that there was not thought to be any threat to the wider public.

CCTV footage time-stamped 07:51 BST on Wednesday shows the suspect appearing to get into a car in Yorkshire, hours before the former Conservative minister is thought to have been attacked in her home.

The man, wearing a white shirt and shorts, appears to have a long object protruding from his shorts pocket.

On Monday, CTPSE confirmed it had taken the lead on the case after new evidence emerged, and was "pursuing multiple lines of enquiry to establish the motivation for this attack".

This video can not be played

CCTV appears to show Widdecombe suspect leave house with object in pocket

Widdecombe's political career spanned decades - she served as MP for Maidstone in Kent for 23 years and worked as a Home Office and employment minister in John Major's government between 1994 and 1997.

Widdecombe was born in Bath, Somerset, in 1947 and went on to study Latin at Birmingham University, then philosophy, politics and economics at Oxford University.

Three years after becoming an MP, she got a foot on the ministerial ladder as a junior social security minister and was then promoted to the employment brief.

In 1995, she was promoted to prisons minister, where she got into a row after defending a policy of chaining pregnant prisoners to prevent them from escaping.

Following the 1997 Labour landslide, she served under William Hague as shadow health secretary between 1998-1999 and shadow home secretary between 1999 - 2001.

After leaving Parliament she embarked on a showbiz career, appearing on Strictly Come Dancing in 2010 and Celebrity Big Brother in 2018.

A staunch supporter of the UK's departure from the EU, Widdecombe became an MEP for the Brexit Party, representing South West England in the European Parliament between 2019 and 2020.

In 2023, Widdecombe joined Reform UK after the party changed its name from the Brexit Party and made a number of appearances as the party's immigration and justice spokesperson.

This video can not be played

Watch: Starmer, Badenoch and Farage respond

Following news of the police investigation, Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer said it was "shocking news" and that his thoughts were with Widdecombe's family "at this awful time".

Conservative leader Kemi Badenoch said she was "stunned" and "really struggled to find the words" in reaction to Widdecombe's death.

Prospective Labour leader Andy Burnham sent his condolences to Widdecombe's family, saying: "Ann gave a lifetime of public service."

Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood urged the public "to avoid speculation and allow the police investigation to progress".

She wrote on X that the circumstances of Widdecombe's death were "extremely distressing", adding that her "thoughts are with Ann's family and loved ones".

Laying a wreath near Widdecombe's home on Saturday, Reform UK's Nigel Farage told reporters she was a "remarkable individual" and "the fiercest defender of free speech".

TV presenter Jeremy Vine paid tribute to Widdecombe on his Channel 5 programme - which she was regular guest on - and was moved to tears when speaking about her death during Monday's episode of his show.

Meanwhile Anton Du Beke, Widdecombe's dance partner on Strictly, said her death was the "saddest of news".

Including allegations of stolen signs, homemade attack flyers, mysterious MAGA figures, and a whole lot of name calling

Renters at Faria Management properties say they're battling mold, rats, sewage leaks, and intimidation. They believe a reckoning for unaccountable landlords is finally here.

With food prices on the rise, these restaurants still provide real value.

A punk show on the Mall, a Palestinian film festival, a Halloween-themed bike ride, and more

The days are getting shorter, the weather is getting colder, and we’re firmly in the grip of spooky season, with events lined up to match. There’s a dark and eerie opera at Wonderland, the annual dog costume contest at Hillwood Estates, a Halloween-themed bike ride on Capitol Hill, and a Backrooms-inspired drag show at the Black Cat.

Not in the mood for spooks and scares? Don’t worry, there’s plenty for you too! There’s a weekend-long celebration of Palestinian art and film, a peek into the inner workings of the Muppets, a punk show at the base of the Washington Monument, and much more going on this weekend.

Artist Talk: (my) favorite📍 Gallery Y (1325 W St. NW)⏰ 6 - 8 p.m.💸 FREEArtists don’t always get to put their own personal favorite works on display, but that’s precisely the theme shared by the work in this exhibit. More than 20 local artists—including photographers, painters, and sculptors—have gathered their most prized pieces for a show at Gallery Y, located inside the YMCA Anthony Bowen. On Thursday night, several artists from the group show will be talking about their work and creative process.

D.C. Palestinian Film & Arts Festival📍 Multiple venues⏰ Thursday to Sunday💸 Prices vary per eventThis weekend marks the 15th annual D.C. Palestinian Film & Arts Festival (DCPFAF), an event that celebrates Palestinian culture and stories through art. The festival kicks off on Thursday evening with a musical performance called “Tarab: Music that Moves Us Forward,” featuring folk and soul music. Throughout the weekend, several films will make their D.C. premieres, including Who Killed Alex Odeh?, which investigates the still-unsolved murder of a Palestinian-American civil rights activist, poet, teacher in 1985. There will also be children’s drawing and storytelling workshops, a bakery pop-up, and more. See the full festival program here.

Opera on Tap DC Metro presents: It's Hallowonderween!📍 Wonderland Ballroom (1101 Kenyon St. NW)⏰ 7 - 9 p.m.💸 FREE, donations welcomeOpera has a long history of haunted castles, ghostly apparitions, and inescapable curses—not to mention one extremely notable phantom. If you want to learn more about the darker side of opera, check out the October installment of Opera on Tap at Wonderland. Seven performers will explore the strange and spooky songs and put a musical twist on what it means to be a scream queen.

Dragrooms📍 Black Cat (1811 14th St. NW)⏰ 8 p.m. doors, 9 p.m. start💸 $19.75Some doors shouldn’t be opened. Others should, like the door to this Backrooms-inspired drag show at the Black Cat. Hosted by Manny Quinn, the show will feature a lineup of local drag talent paying homage to analog horror and liminal spaces. See how far it goes.

Jim Henson: A Creative Life in Six Objects📍 National Museum of American History (14th St. & Constitution Ave. NW)⏰ 12 - 1:30 p.m.💸 $20 for members, $30 general admissionAmong the vast archives of the Smithsonian are dozens of puppets and props from legendary puppeteer Jim Henson, including the original Kermit the Frog and Oscar the Grouch’s trash can. At this lecture, Jim Henson Company archives director Karen Falk and biographer Brian Jay Jones will explore six extraordinary objects from the collection, from early experiments to iconic creations. Following the program, attendees will get a rare opportunity to see objects from the National Museum of American History’s collection that aren’t on public display.

Movie Night: Clue (1985)📍 Dandelion Collective DC (3417 14th St. NW)⏰ 6:30 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. start💸 FREEIn honor of the late great Tim Curry, the Fanthropologist is hosting a screening of Clue. Based on the board game of the same name, this cult classic finds six colorful dinner guests gathered at the mansion of Mr. Boddy — who was blackmailing all of them and winds up dead. With the killer among them, the guests and Boddy’s butler (played by Curry) have to figure out who did it.

Seven Readings: Comedy and Stories from the Great Unknown📍 Rhizome DC (6950 Maple St. NW⏰ 6:30 p.m. doors, 7 p.m. start💸 $17.19Each of the performers at this Basement Cabaret event received a tarot reading earlier this month. They have spent the last few weeks translating those readings into works of storytelling, comedy sets, burlesque acts, or films. It’s a celebration of intuition, creativity, and performance. Come see the final products from more than a dozen performers.

Pop-up Trivia on the Farm 📍 Edgewood Community Farm (2304 2nd St. NE)⏰ 7 - 9 p.m.💸 FREELooking for farm-to-table trivia? Edgewood Community Farm promises that the questions at its pop-up trivia night are all-natural — no AI-generated questions or generic canned trivia in sight. Categories include general trivia, music, mash-ups, and whatever else they’re in the mood for. Bring a team or show up solo and make some new friends. The event is BYOB and BYO-snacks.

Sofar So Spooky📍 Living Room DC (3169 Mt Pleasant St. NW, upstairs)⏰ 7:30 p.m. doors, 8 p.m. start💸 $31Join Sofar Sounds for a special Halloween-themed show. Precise details about the show will be a mystery until just before it starts, but Sofar promises an intimate show filled with eerie tunes, seasonal decor, and more. The event is BYOB (except for red wine) and small snacks are allowed.

Growing Community: Fall Garden Day📍 Anacostia Community Museum (1901 Fort Pl. SE)⏰ 10 a.m. - 12 p.m.💸 FREENow that it’s feeling like fall, mark the seasonal change with gardening, storytelling, and lessons for the season ahead. Head to the Anacostia Community Museum to celebrate the end of the growing season and learn how to transition a garden to fall and winter. This can be a time for reflection and planning for the future — the event will include journaling and opportunities to share stories and knowledge with other gardeners.

Carnegie Science Earth & Planets Laboratory Open House📍 Carnegie Science Earth & Planets Laboratory (5241 Broad Branch Rd. NW)⏰ 1 - 4 p.m.💸 FREEFor the second year in a row, the Carnegie Science Earth & Planets Laboratory (EPL) is opening its doors to the public. Scientists at EPL study everything from the rocks beneath our feet to the stars above. They’ll have a ton of science activities, from building your own spectrometer to touching a real-life meteorite. Turnstile at the Washington Monument📍 Sylvan Theater (Independence Ave. SW & 15th St. NW)⏰ 3 p.m.💸 FREE, donations encouragedWhat’s more punk than the Washington Monument? Los Angeles fire officials were grilled Friday over plans to spend $345 million a year from a proposed sales tax hike, as the department revealed more than half its stations are past their expected lifespan and crews can’t reach most city streets within the recommended four minutes.

With just 11 days before voters decide the fate of Measure FD, Councilwoman Traci Park and fellow councilmembers pressed Fire Chief Jaime Moore over how the department would spend the cash, fix fire stations and get more firefighters on the streets without wasting taxpayer dollars.

“If we are asking Angelenos to invest hundreds of millions of dollars into the fire department, City Hall owes them a concrete plan for how every dollar is going to make LA safer,” Park said.

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

Park noted that the LAFD is operating with a budget approaching $1 billion, with its proposed 2026-27 spending plan totaling $939.5 million. The proposed half-cent sales tax hike would pump another $345 million annually into the department, potentially pushing its funding to nearly $1.3 billion.

But the department’s laundry list of problems is staggering.

Moore testified that 56 of LA’s 106 fire stations are between 50 and 85 years old, while six of the 22 maintenance hoists used to repair fire trucks at its Lincoln Heights facility are broken.

And buying new fire engines won’t deliver an overnight fix.

“It takes about three years for us to get a new fire engine,” Moore told the council.

The department’s own analysis found its fire engines and ambulances can reach just 49.2% of city roads within four minutes, the recommended response-time benchmark.

LAFD has roughly the same number of firefighters as it did in the 1960s, despite emergency call volumes multiplying and the city’s population surging by 1.4 million people, according to firefighters who testified Friday.

Moore outlined plans to expand the next two firefighter recruit classes from a combined 120 to 180 recruits, but acknowledged the department doesn’t have enough civilian workers to process applicants or sufficient training infrastructure to rapidly expand hiring.

“We’re gonna have to hire more civilian staff,” Moore told council members, explaining that years of budget cuts had depleted the department’s support workforce.

Park zeroed in on whether City Hall could be trusted to keep the new tax money from disappearing into other spending priorities.

“Chief, are there mechanisms in place to prevent the Measure FD funds from being absorbed into the city’s general fund or being diverted for purposes other than fire department expansion?” she asked.

Moore said the measure includes protections preventing the revenue from being diverted to other city programs.

The United Firefighters of Los Angeles City union has already poured $4.5 million of its members’ money into campaigning for Measure FD, according to union secretary Ryan Quigley.

The proposal would raise LA’s sales tax from 10.25% to 10.75%, with no expiration date.

Park’s motion demands a detailed spending plan outlining which fire stations and equipment would be prioritized, how quickly additional firefighters could be hired and what improvements taxpayers could expect within 30, 60, 90 and 180 days.

The Trump administration is demanding an emergency court order to stop California from counting ballots tied to more than 20,000 suspected noncitizens, warning that once the votes are mixed in, there may be no way to undo it.

First Assistant US Attorney Bill Essayli and Attorney General Todd Blanche are leading the Justice Department’s push for the 9th Circuit Court of Appeals to force California to set aside the disputed mail-in ballots and verify voters’ citizenship before counting them.

“Every minute that goes by, American citizen votes are being diluted in the state of California,” Essayli said Thursday. “It’s an emergency, and we expect the courts to treat it as such.”

The biggest news, opinion and culture shaping California right now.

Please provide a valid email.

By clicking above you agree to the Terms of Use and Privacy Policy.

Never miss a story

The DOJ says it identified more than 20,000 people who are registered to vote in California, received mail-in ballots and are considered highly likely to be noncitizens. Federal law prohibits noncitizens from voting in federal elections, and the government says some people have already been criminally charged over alleged illegal registration and voting.

“We’re not asking California to take any drastic steps other than to sequester the ballots from the suspected noncitizens,” Essayli told Fox News. “We believe it’s at a minimum of 20,000. That’s the floor.”

The emergency motion warns that Los Angeles County has already processed more than 331,000 mail-in ballots. Once election workers separate ballots from their envelopes, the government argues, identifying individual voters becomes impossible — making it critical to keep potentially ineligible ballots separate before they are counted.

The administration is asking the appeals court to order California to segregate the ballots and verify citizenship before tabulation. It is seeking a ruling by Saturday, Oct. 24.

The motion names California, Secretary of State Shirley N. Weber and Los Angeles County Registrar-Recorder/County Clerk Dean C. Logan as defendants. California and Weber oppose the request.

The appeal follows US District Judge David O. Carter’s failure to rule on the administration’s emergency request by its demanded deadline.

The DOJ argues the delay effectively denied its bid for immediate relief.

Gov. Gavin Newsom has said California follows applicable federal election laws.

hochul-letitia-james-cornell:
By now the story has gripped the nation: A former Cornell student, known as Jane Doe, has accused seven frat members of raping her two years ago. Nobody was initially charged because Doe told school officials she consented to the sexual acts, but two years later, Doe has changed her account of the events and claims she was incapable of consenting.

Days after the Cornell 7 story broke, New York’s sitting Attorney General Letitia James weighed in on the allegations, treating them as though they were fact.

In a tweet on September 28, James wrote: “What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers. To her, and to all survivors, you’re not alone. We stand with you.”

Days after this post, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul tapped James to look into the case.

But during a press briefing on Friday, a reporter asked why Hochul appointed “an official who made a public statement affirming those allegations as fact as someone who’s supposed to be doing an investigation?”

Hochul disregarded the very legitimate concern that James is already a biased party in the story and instead said she is confident that James will “do what she has always done. Look at the facts, examine the record, and draw the proper conclusions. That’s exactly what’s going to happen in this case.”

But if James is doing “what she has always done,” then the Cornell 7 aren’t going to get a fair and impartial trial. They’re going to get (metaphorically) the gulag.

James spent months using lawfare to try and kneecap then-candidate Donald Trump ahead of the 2024 election. James accused Trump of inflating his personal wealth to get more favorable loan terms. Notably, there were no victims in the case and a court later found the judgment against Trump to be unconstitutional. The case was so political that even CNN political commentator Jonah Goldberg called the “prosecution … a mistake” and “very political.”

Former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo argued the case was also the result of political lawfare.

“If his name was not Donald Trump, and if he wasn’t running for president, I’m the former AG in New York, I’m telling you that case would have never been brought, and that’s what is offensive to people,” Cuomo said during a June 2024 appearance on Real Time with Bill Maher: Overtime.

But it was no surprise that James brought the case, having campaigned on using lawfare to target Trump and calling him an “illegitimate president.” As The Federalist’s Matt Kittle reported, a prosecutor in James’ office even said he was ordered to target Trump, which is why Hochul’s assurance that James will “do what she has always done” is problematic.

James declared Trump illegitimate, campaigned with a promise to target him, and then brought a case so obviously political that even prominent Democrats questioned it. James has already publicly treated the Cornell allegations as fact being tasked with investigating it. If her past is any indication, the Cornell 7 have every reason to fear an investigation will seek not justice, but to validate James’ prejudgment.

factcheck_hochul-letitia-james-cornell:
By now the story has gripped the nation: A former Cornell student, known as Jane Doe, has accused seven frat members of raping her two years ago. Nobody was initially charged because Doe told school officials she consented to the sexual acts, but two years later, Doe has changed her account of the events and claims she was incapable of consenting.

Days after the Cornell 7 story broke, New York’s sitting Attorney General Letitia James weighed in on the allegations, treating them as though they were fact.

In a tweet on September 28, James wrote: “What this young woman has been forced to endure is horrific and unacceptable. I’m holding her in my heart and in my prayers. To her, and to all survivors, you’re not alone. We stand with you.”

Days after this post, New York Gov. Kathy Hochul tapped James to look into the case.

But during a press briefing on Friday, a reporter asked why Hochul appointed “an official who made a public statement affirming those allegations as fact as someone who’s supposed to be doing an investigation?”

Hochul disregarded the very legitimate concern that James is already a biased party in the story and instead said she is confident that James will “do what she has always done. Look at the facts, examine the record, and draw the proper conclusions. That’s exactly what’s going to happen in this case.”

But if James is doing “what she has always done,” then the Cornell 7 aren’t going to get a fair and impartial trial. They’re going to get (metaphorically) the gulag.

James spent months using lawfare to try and kneecap then-candidate Donald Trump ahead of the 2024 election. James accused Trump of inflating his personal wealth to get more favorable loan terms. Notably, there were no victims in the case and a court later found the judgment against Trump to be unconstitutional. The case was so political that even CNN political commentator Jonah Goldberg called the “prosecution … a mistake” and “very political.”

Former New York Gov. Andrew Cuomo argued the case was also the result of political lawfare.

“If his name was not Donald Trump, and if he wasn’t running for president, I’m the former AG in New York, I’m telling you that case would have never been brought, and that’s what is offensive to people,” Cuomo said during a June 2024 appearance on Real Time with Bill Maher: Overtime.

But it was no surprise that James brought the case, having campaigned on using lawfare to target Trump and calling him an “illegitimate president.” As The Federalist’s Matt Kittle reported, a prosecutor in James’ office even said he was ordered to target Trump, which is why Hochul’s assurance that James will “do what she has always done” is problematic.

James declared Trump illegitimate, campaigned with a promise to target him, and then brought a case so obviously political that even prominent Democrats questioned it. James has already publicly treated the Cornell allegations as fact being tasked with investigating it. If her past is any indication, the Cornell 7 have every reason to fear an investigation will seek not justice, but to validate James’ prejudgment.

deadly-shooting-jordan-church-hamoud:
(AP) A man looks through a gap in a stone wall toward a Greek Orthodox church where gunmen opened fire during a funeral hours earlier in Jordan's Hamoud village on Friday, Oct. 23, 2026.

Comment

Add as Preferred Source

Gunmen opened fire at a Greek Orthodox church in southern Jordan on Friday, killing at least seven people and wounding nearly three dozen others, in what Jordanian officials called a terrorist attack.

Prime Minister Jafar Hassan said at a news conference the attack was “the result of terrorist takfiri ideology,” referring to a view that effectively allows one Muslim to declare another an apostate. How that figured into an attack on a Christian church was not immediately clear.

By Friday night, a hunt for the attackers was still underway, and no group had claimed responsibility.

The shooting, one of the deadliest attacks in Jordan in years, took place during a funeral in Karak province, which is home to a sizable Christian community, Maj. Gen. Obaidallah Maaytah said at an earlier news conference.

The unidentified attackers emerged from a vehicle and opened fire in the village of Hamoud, according to Jordan’s state broadcaster, Al Mamlaka, which showed security camera footage that appeared to show three men firing toward the church from the street before running toward the building.

Jordan’s interior minister, Mazin Farrayeh, said that the attack had been carried out by “extremists.” He did not identify them or any affiliation they had, saying an investigation was underway.

King Abdullah II vowed the attack would be met with “the harshest retaliation.”

“Those who delude themselves into thinking that they can divide Jordanians with their bullets,” he said on social media, “have no chance in the face of our unity.”

Jordan has largely avoided the violence that has destabilized many of its neighbors, though it has faced sporadic militant attacks over the past decade, and at one time it hosted more than a million refugees from the Syrian civil war. In 2016, Islamic State militants killed 10 people in a shooting rampage in and around the city of Karak before taking shelter in a medieval castle there.

The Christian presence in Karak dates back more than 1,500 years, to a time when the Eastern Roman Empire ruled this part of the Middle East. Today, Christians make up about 2% of Jordan’s population, but they are guaranteed seats in Parliament and have long served as Cabinet ministers and ambassadors.

Note to readers • This article originally appeared in The New York Times.

LDS Church leaders express sympathy

The Middle East-Africa North Area Presidency of The Church of Jesus Christ of Latter-day Saints issued a statement late Friday expressing sympathy to those affected by the shooting in Jordan.

“We are saddened by the tragedy that took place at St. George Greek Orthodox Church in Karak Governorate of the Hashemite Kingdom of Jordan,” the statement said.

“We express our love and support and grieve with those affected by this tragedy at this place of worship. Our deepest sympathies are with the families of the victims,” the leaders said. “We pray for the recovery of those who are injured and for those currently caring for and assisting the hospitalized. Our prayers are for peace, comfort and healing for all who are mourning and suffering as a result of this tragic event.”

10-years-later-fact-checker-glenn-kessle:
Kessler said he’s never made a mistake that needed retraction.

WASHINGTON, D.C. — Former Washington Post “fact checker” Glenn Kessler was awarded the “Philip J. Klass Award for outstanding promotion of critical thinking and scientific understanding” Thursday night. But when confronted with his persistent Russia collusion hoax propaganda, Kessler insisted “there is no Russia collusion hoax.”

Kessler was given the award by a group called the National Capital Area Skeptics at an event titled “Fact-Checking in a World of Misinformation” in the Media and Public Affairs Building of George Washington University.

The Federalist has extensively tracked Kessler’s career of partisan deception, which includes lying about Russian collusion and the bogus Steele dossier, refusing to consider evidence that the coronavirus leaked from a Chinese lab, altering statements about election integrity to fit the narrative of a “fact check,” waving off concerns about the coronavirus shot, and much more.

Kessler also leaned into his mathematically absurd claim that President Donald Trump had said “over 30,000” false or misleading statements in his first term, 16,000 of which came in the first three years and 14,000 of which came in the final year.

Meanwhile, Kessler admitted at the GW event he actively refused the same treatment for President Joe Biden, stating, “I was injured by Trump. I had to go through four months of physical therapy … when Biden came in, they wanted me to do it for Biden. I said, ‘I’ll do 100 days for Biden. I’m not going to do anything more.'”

Interviewer Joel Achenbach, a former staff writer/science journalist at The Washington Post, told him “obviously, you did a heroic job for years, in what had to been an exhausting job too, particularly after 2016.”

When asked by The Federalist if he was worried “fact checkers” have lost their credibility after perpetuating the Russia collusion hoax and cooperating with social media companies to censor Americans who countered approved narratives about Covid, Kessler became extremely defensive.

He attempted to explain away the hoax by pointing to the Senate Intelligence Committee report stating Russia attempted to interfere with the 2016 election, but that entirely alters the claim that “fact-checkers” like Kessler had been making all along.

When confronted by the fact that the hoax that he perpetuated falsely asserted Trump colluded with the Russians to alter the election, and asked if he has read the documents showing the hoax was a concoction of the Obama administration to kneecap Trump, Kessler became exasperated.

“I’m sorry, just to be frank, what you’re saying you’re repeating things that are simply false,” he asserted. When pushed again on if he had actually read the documents, he responded with an annoyed “yes.”

“This is a great example of the kind of strange, you know, partisan mindsets that that you know people that aren’t thinking critically will accept. But those things are not true,” he added.

A GW student journalist in the room seemed to find it ironic that the person talking about objectivity and critical thinking skills was wholly incapable of participating in the very thing he was advocating, stating in a passed note, “He could not deal with any criticism — so typical!”

Kessler’s refrain that “it is increasingly a world of misinformation, and it is indeed getting worse,” stood in stark contrast to the mountains of evidence that the entire narrative was a fabrication.

Achenbach asked Kessler whether he’d ever made any major errors, and Kessler said he had not — only some partial missteps that prove “no fact check is ever finished.”

“There was never any thing that I recall where we had to retract the article or anything like that,” Kessler said. “You know, I always said, you know, no fact check is ever finished, and we update with new information.”

But the “fact checking” industry is continuing to lose credibility. Just this week, the “fact checkers” were again proven to be unquestioning shills of their Democrat friends, as even more evidence comes out suggesting Rep. Ilhan Omar really did marry her brother and allegedly committed immigration fraud. Snopes, another “fact checker” rated this claim “unfounded.”

As The Federalist’s Mark Hemingway observed, “that ‘fact checkers’ tried to make their judgments on complicated matters of rhetoric and policy sound definitive to the point of pseudoscientific objectivity was always absurd … The first Trump presidency made it painfully obvious that ‘fact checking’ did not exist as a fair and independent vocation. It was strictly an attempt to control the public debate.”

In his dubious defense of “truth,” “objectivity,” “critical thinking,” and the rest, Kessler ended the night by decrying the hyper-partisanship of American discourse, which he blamed entirely on Trump because he was apparently the first to break the dam on saying “the other side is evil.” Achenbach dutifully agreed, stating, “Trump changed the tone of what you’re allowed to say.”

But while Achenbach made some attempt to say political rancor had plagued American discourse since the founding, which is true, Kessler, with all his objectivity, blamed first and foremost Trum, and then the House speakership of Newt Gingrich in the mid-1990s.

True to form, Kessler happened to omit the fact that Democrats have been calling Republicans “Nazis,” a synonym for evil in the Western political lexicon, since the 1940s.

In 1948, just three years after World War II, President Harry Truman likened Republican presidential nominee Thomas Dewey to Adolf Hitler directly. The same happened in 1964 with Republican presidential nominee Barry Goldwater, while President Lyndon Johnson said a Goldwater presidency would bring about American nuclear holocaust. The invective was extended to Presidents Richard Nixon, Ronald Reagan, and George W. Bush, as well as Republican nominee Mitt Romney.

Trump has had it worse than all of those Republicans combined.

While those are just presidents or presidential candidates, the trend trickles down to all levels of Republican candidacy. What it has achieved, which Kessler seemed intent on papering over, is the wave of left-wing violence that has been unleashed in recent years, which has no counterpart on the right.

From the assassination of Charlie Kirk, to the shooting of Trump, to the shooting of congressional Republicans at baseball practice, to the Black Lives Matter riots, and much more, the rhetoric has achieved its intended result.

Every time, Democrat politicians are given cover by the corporate media, including the fact checkers like Kessler, to continue their push toward violence.

The Biden administration’s Department of Homeland Security (DHS) scheduled Pride Month events during government working hours, including a pansexual forum and LGBTQ educational videos at a federal law enforcement training center, according to records obtained exclusively by the Daily Caller News Foundation.

The 20-page June 2023 calendar details planned events at FEMA, the Secret Service, immigration agencies and other DHS components, according to documents obtained through a Freedom of Information Act request by the Center to Advance Security in America (CASA). President Donald Trump subsequently ordered federal agencies to dismantle diversity, equity and inclusion (DEI) programs, raising questions about whether the activities documented in the records continued under his administration.

The DCNF asked DHS whether it had discontinued the Biden-era Pride Month programming, whether similar events occurred in 2025 or 2026, and what policy changes the Trump administration implemented regarding DEI initiatives and employee activities. The White House referred to the DHS, which did not respond to a request for comment.

“The Biden DHS failed the country in many ways, and part of the reason for its failure was its focus on non-mission-oriented activities such as these,” James Fitzpatrick, director of CASA, told the DCNF. (RELATED: EXCLUSIVE: Unearthed Data Sheds Light On Military’s Transgenderism Explosion Under Biden)

For the past three years, we have raised the Pride Progress flag at the @DHSgov headquarters to recognize the start of #PrideMonth. Today, we continue this tradition – a symbol of our commitment to stand with our LGBTQ+ colleagues and the community with pride. https://t.co/O3J5gwGDXs

Trump directed federal agencies to terminate covered DEI programs on Jan. 20, 2025, according to the White House. The following day, the Office of Personnel Management (OPM) instructed agencies to close diversity, equity, inclusion and accessibility (DEIA) offices and cancel related training, according to OPM.

FEMA Pride scheduled a “Bisexual and Pansexual Forum” for June 13, 2023, from 2:00 to 3:00 p.m., according to the DHS records provided by CASA. The agency also listed a transgender and gender-nonconforming forum on June 20, an intersex forum on June 22 and an asexual forum on June 27, all scheduled for the afternoon.

FEMA and OPM did not respond to requests for comment.

The Federal Law Enforcement Training Centers (FLETC) planned a June 27 video watch party and discussion at 11:00 a.m. Eastern, according to the records obtained by CASA. The schedule listed videos titled “A Living History of the LGBT Movement Since the 1800s” and “LGBTQ+ 101: An introduction to Queer community.”

At DHS headquarters in Washington, D.C., the calendar included a June 2 Pride flag-raising ceremony with then-Secretary Alejandro Mayorkas and Deputy Secretary John Tien. Photographs released by DHS confirm both officials attended the ceremony, according to the department. The Secret Service and U.S. Citizenship and Immigration Services also planned a June 7 program featuring a speaker described as the first intersex and transgender graduate of the Secret Service’s Law Enforcement Officer Academy, according to the records provided by CASA. The speaker’s name was redacted in the released documents.

The Secret Service did not respond to a request for comment.

Immigration and Customs Enforcement listed a June 22 virtual “Lunch and Learn” session on transgender employees in the workplace, according to the DHS schedule. Other entries covered Pride celebrations, employee newsletters, displays and participation in public parades across several DHS components, according to records obtained by CASA.

Some calendar entries included specific business-hour times, while others were marked “time TBD” or simply “month of June,” according to the records. Authorities in Tucson, Arizona, arrested several minors Tuesday on charges related to the burglary of a city gun store, according to local media.

The Pima County Sheriff’s Department stated that the juveniles were involved in an Oct. 8 burglary at SNG Tactical during which a vehicle was rammed into the gun store, KVOA TV, a Tucson-area TV station reported Tuesday. The burglaries at federally-licensed firearms dealers (FFLs) had prompted at least one to place his truck in a blocking position to prevent ramming attacks at his store. (RELATED: Gun Store Owner Puts His Truck On The Line To Stop Crooks)

Multiple juveniles between the ages of 14 and 17 have been arrested, and several stolen firearms have been recovered following a burglary at SNG Tactical. https://t.co/MUvaQf7RGH

John Petrush, the owner of John’s Guns and Ammo in Tucson, told the station that a local police officer recommended the measure since one of the shops targeted was located very near Petrush’s store. Petrush also predicted that police would find the perpetrators in an Oct. 9 report by KVOA regarding the burglaries.

“They’re always going to slip somewhere, whether it be a camera that catches them or just somebody walking by that’s seen something, Petrush said. “And if they come and say something, the likelihood is more so of them getting caught.”

Pima County sheriff’s deputies and agents of the Bureau of Alcohol, Tobacco, Firearms and Explosives (ATF) worked on the investigation. Possession of a stolen firearm is a federal crime and can lead to a ten-year sentence in federal prison.

unholy-alliance-gambling-news:
Photo by Spencer Platt/Getty Images)

The unholy alliance between the gambling industry and news organizations is growing deeper.

As part of a new sponsorship agreement with the gambling giant DraftKings, local news stations owned by CBS News must air four DraftKings “hits” per day between Oct. 26 and Nov. 3, according to an exclusive report from Status. The deal frustrated some executives, who believed the optics of mixing gambling and news coverage could undermine faith in elections, Status reported. (RELATED: CNN Just Cracked Open Pandora’s Box That’s Worse Than Any Fake News Hoax)

CBS News is not the first media organization to partner with the gambling industry.

In late 2025, CNN announced a partnership with the prediction market company Kalshi. A day later, CNBC announced a similar deal.

“CNBC will incorporate exclusive Kalshi predictions market data into its programs, including ‘Squawk Box’ and ‘Fast Money,’ offering viewers a unique perspective on how event forecasts and probabilities are shifting in real time. A Kalshi ticker will run alongside segments of CNBC’s on-air programming. Kalshi will also launch a CNBC page on its site, featuring CNBC-selected markets,” the network said.

The Associated Press also partnered with Kalshi in March.

“The Associated Press for nearly two centuries has played an essential role in American democracy as the most authoritative source for accurate results on election night,” David Scott, vice president for AP Elections, said. “We’re pleased to be working with Kalshi as we work to expand the reach of AP’s trusted elections data, meeting audiences where they are with reliable information about who voters have chosen to lead their country and communities.” (RELATED: Special Forces Soldier Accused Of Gambling On Maduro Raid Pleads Not Guilty)

Meanwhile, The Wall Street Journal has struck a deal with Kalshi’s competitor, Polymarket.

“We’re making prediction markets data accessible to our users, because it’s a rapidly growing source of real-time insight into collective beliefs about future events,” Almar Latour, CEO of Dow Jones and publisher of The Wall Street Journal, said. “Our mission is to help people make decisions by offering them reliable news, data and analysis. In partnering with Polymarket, we aim to help consumers better interpret market sentiment and assess risk alongside traditional financial indicators.”

Critics argue that because prediction markets allow traders to wager on something as simple as whether a CNN host will say a particular word during a broadcast, the partnership opens up a Pandora’s box of ethical concerns. Reporters and broadcasters, for example, could cover a breaking news event in a way that benefits a wager they made on one of the partnering platforms.

A CBS News spokesman told Status that the sponsorship deal is strictly commercial and will have no effect on its editorial decisions or election coverage.

benjamin-netanyahu-signals-massive-west-:
Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced Friday that Israel is preparing a massive military operation in Judea and Samaria, also known as the West Bank, on a scale not seen since the 1967 Six-Day War, after Palestinian terrorists killed two Israeli soldiers near Hebron, just four days before Israel’s national election.

Speaking after a security assessment, Netanyahu said the planned operation would be unprecedented in scope.

“The defense minister and I have overseen the planning of a very extensive IDF operation in Judea and Samaria — on a scale not seen since the Six-Day War,” he said.

“The IDF is ready to carry it out, and we will determine the timing, but it is coming.”

The announcement followed a deadly shooting at a temporary military checkpoint near Yehuda Junction outside Hebron, where two Palestinian terrorists opened fire on Israeli soldiers Friday morning.

The attack killed Staff Sgt. Ron Yonatan Roytman, 23, of Ashkelon, and Sgt. Yuval Shai Svilem, 20, of Hod Hasharon, both members of the Israel Defense Forces’ (IDF) 775th Ari Battalion. Three additional soldiers were wounded.

Israeli forces killed both attackers following a firefight lasting more than 20 minutes.

The IDF’s preliminary investigation found that the terrorists apparently intended to attack Israeli civilians along a nearby highway but instead opened fire on soldiers after encountering the checkpoint.

The military said the attackers were carrying substantial quantities of ammunition, suggesting they had planned a larger assault.

Netanyahu said Israel would adopt the aggressive counterterrorism approach previously used against terrorist strongholds in West Bank refugee camps.

“We will evacuate the residents, go from house to house, remove the weapons there, and address and demolish all terrorist infrastructure,” he said.

The prime minister ordered security forces to seal off Hebron and prepare for a broader lockdown across Judea and Samaria, while the IDF deployed additional troops and launched arrest operations.

IDF Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir confirmed that the military had reinforced the region with the headquarters of its 98th Division and additional forces.

“Based on the situational assessment, we prepared for the possibility of escalation in Judea and Samaria, reinforced our troops, and deployed the 98th Division headquarters and numerous additional troops to the area,” Zamir said.

Meanwhile, IDF Central Command chief Maj. Gen. Avi Bluth announced that Israeli forces were launching a significant counterterrorism operation while cordoning off Hebron and nearby Halhul.

“A grave terror attack against Israeli civilians was thwarted” through the soldiers’ actions, Bluth said, while acknowledging the deaths of the two servicemen.

Israeli authorities also began demolishing unauthorized structures near Hebron, with Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich announcing that heavy machinery was already operating in the area.

The military measures come ahead of Israel’s national election on Tuesday, October 27, amid warnings from Netanyahu and senior defense officials that hostile forces could attempt to carry out attacks during the final days of the campaign.

“We warned several weeks ago about attempts by our enemies to harm us, our civilians and our soldiers ahead of the elections,” Netanyahu said Friday. “That is what they tried to do here.”

Defense Minister Israel Katz also warned that Iran and its terrorist proxies were seeking to influence Tuesday’s election through attacks, although Israeli authorities have not established that Tehran directed Friday’s shooting.

Hamas praised the attack but did not formally claim responsibility, while Israeli security agencies continued investigating whether the two terrorists operated independently or were connected to a larger terrorist network.

Netanyahu has not announced when the broader offensive will begin, leaving the timing of what he described as Israel’s most extensive West Bank military operation since 1967 unresolved as the country heads into Tuesday’s national election.

Joshua Klein is a reporter for Breitbart News. Email him at jklein@breitbart.com. Follow him on Twitter @JoshuaKlein.

goldman-sachs-ai-small-business:
Goldman Sachs CEO David Solomon unveiled a $500 million commitment to bring AI training to small business owners at the launch of the bank’s new Small Business AI Institute on Thursday.

Fortune reports that Solomon announced Goldman Sachs’ commitment alongside four technology partners: Anthropic, Google, Meta and OpenAI. The money will fund the next phase of Goldman’s 10,000 Small Businesses program, which has graduated nearly 20,000 entrepreneurs since it launched in 2010 as part of an earlier $1.25 billion pledge. The next chapter will focus on education, access to capital and support services.

Solomon said small businesses make up 99 percent of U.S. businesses, calling them a “hugely important ecosystem.” The new institute has three parts: training and learning programs run by each partner company, research into how small businesses use AI, and expanded access to capital.

Each partner has a different job. Anthropic will build a learning series on applied AI for small businesses, run hands-on workshops for program alumni and research how small businesses use AI. Google will give nearly 20,000 small-business owners and employees its Grow with Google AI Professional certificate, plus three months of free access to Google AI Pro. Meta will offer AI tools and training through Muse for Small Business. OpenAI will run AI workshops through the program’s community college partners.

Solomon urged small-business owners not to rush. “At the moment, this is an expensive technology,” he said, adding, “I don’t think that you have to look at the world and say, ‘I’ve got to be the best at this, I have to have this figured out in the next three weeks.'” He framed adoption as a question of return on investment in areas like sales, customer experience, manufacturing and procurement: “If you think about token costs and you think about the cost of being on these platforms, the return can come from productivity.” His advice, he said, was simple: “The important thing is to get it right, not to get it quicker.”

Solomon also drew a line between the cutting edge of AI development and what small businesses actually need. “Frontier models and how frontier models develop is going to be a very, very interesting thing,” he said, noting that “the technology is moving very, very quickly, and the technology is going to continue to move quickly.” Still, he said, “there’s very little that we do where we need frontier models.” He added that “you have to separate at some level” the “bigger picture frontier issues that are getting a lot of attention” from “using the base tools that exist to support your businesses.” He also pointed to capital as an ongoing hurdle: “Access to capital continues to be a constraint.” On AI’s effect on staffing, he said it can let an owner take on more strategic work without hiring outside help: “it’s not limiting the job, but it’s creating more leverage in the business without a fixed cost base.”

Breitbart News recently reported that banks are working quickly to prevent rogue AI agents from accessing the bank accounts of their unwitting human users:

Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, JPMorgan, Wells Fargo and other large banks are finding AI agents inside accounts that, in some cases, appear to be taking actions the account holder never actually told them to take. One bank official called the situation “horrifying.” Another described “grave concerns about agents gaining access to customer accounts and taking steps that could impact user finances.”

Unwanted AI access to accounts typically occurs when a customer hands their login credentials to an AI assistant so it can manage part of their financial life, then gives it access to the account. That already breaks most banks’ rules, which require a human to log in directly. The real danger shows up when a user has also authorized the agent to make purchases or move money. Combine that permission with login access, and the agent can act on its own, with nobody watching.

AI presents both opportunities to improve the performance of small businesses, as well as massive landmines like negative impacts on mental health and your bank balance. Breitbart News social media director Wynton Hall has written his New York Times bestseller Code Red: The Left, the Right, China, and the Race to Control AI to serve as the definitive guide on how the MAGA movement can create positions on AI that benefit humanity without handing control of our nation to the leftists of Silicon Valley or allowing the Chinese to take over the world.

Read more at Fortune here.

Lucas Nolan is a reporter for Breitbart News covering issues of AI, free speech, and online censorship.
